transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because... for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take me seriously. It's about my job. The new ticket rotation system and these security audits they keep running—they're being used to build a paper trail against me. I mean, management keeps showing me the system logs and telling me it’s just standard policy, but... well, I know what's happening. So, I guess I'm here because I just need someone to look at this and listen to what's really going on.
Have you ever been able to consider that there might be another explanation for what’s happening at work?

I mean... I've tried to look at it that way. I really have. But... well, like I said, for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. 

Management sits me down, they show me the system logs, and they keep telling me it’s just standard policy. But I've been doing computer support a long time. I know how the new ticket rotation is set up, and I see exactly how these security audits are running. They’re being used to build a paper trail against me. So, no... I can't just accept that it's a coincidence or just normal procedure, because I can see exactly what they're doing, even if they keep hiding behind company policy.
Have you ever heard voices that other people could not hear?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or anything. My hearing is fine, and I only hear what's actually there. My issue isn't... it's not in my head like that. It's right there in the system logs and the ticket assignments.
Have you generally been suspicious and mistrustful of other people since you were a young adult?

No, not really. I mean, I've always been a pretty normal guy. I trust people just fine when they give me a reason to. I've had good friends, good relationships with coworkers over the years... until this started happening at my current job. So, no, I wouldn't say I've been suspicious my whole life. It's just this specific situation with management and the ticket system.
Has anyone else at work or in your life told you that your belief about management building a paper trail against you is not true?

No, not really. I... I don't exactly go around broadcasting this to my family or the other techs on the floor. It's a professional issue, so I mostly just keep it between me and the management team. 

So, besides them trying to tell me it's just standard policy, like I mentioned earlier... no. Nobody else has told me it's not true, mostly because I just haven't brought it up for them to weigh in on.
Do you believe the people at work are specifically targeting you because of a larger, implausible plan or special message directed at you, rather than just ordinary workplace retaliation?

No, no, it's nothing like that. There's no grand conspiracy or secret message or anything crazy. I'm just a computer support specialist, you know? I'm not that important in the grand scheme of things. 

It's just standard, petty workplace politics. They want me gone, probably to hire someone younger or cheaper, and they're using the ticket system to build a case against me so they can fire me with cause. It's just... ordinary retaliation, like you said. Nothing more to it than that.
During the times when you’ve felt convinced management is targeting you, have you also had periods of feeling unusually energized or needing much less sleep than usual?

No, not at all. I mean, if anything, dealing with all this extra scrutiny is just exhausting. I definitely don't feel unusually energized. 

I sleep my normal amount... well, maybe I toss and turn a bit if I'm lying awake worrying about my job, but I definitely still need the sleep. I'm 60 years old, I need my rest to function. So, no, nothing like that. Just my regular routine, just a lot more stressful lately.
Have you become more socially withdrawn or less interested in other people than you used to be?

No, not really. I mean, I still see my family on the weekends, and I still talk to the few friends I've had for years. I haven't stopped doing any of that. 

I guess I might be a little quieter at work, just because I'm trying to keep my head down and not give them any more ammunition, but outside of that? No. I'm still just as interested in seeing people as I ever was. I'm just a normal guy, just dealing with a bad situation at the office.
Have you ever believed that people outside of work were also watching, following, or trying to harm you?

No, never. It's strictly a work thing. I don't feel like anyone is following me home or watching my house or anything like that. When I leave the office, I leave it behind. It's just the management at the company trying to push me out, nobody else.
Have you had this belief about your job for at least six months?

Yes, definitely longer than six months. It's been going on since they rolled out the new hybrid schedule and made those changes to how we handle after-hours tickets. That was... let's see, about a year and two months ago now. So yeah, it's been happening for well over a year.
Have you ever heard a voice or voices speaking to you when no one else was around?

No, I haven't. I've never heard voices or anything like that. I just hear the normal office chatter and the things they say when they think I'm not listening. But no, if I'm alone, it's quiet. I don't hear things that aren't there.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast to other people, inserted into your mind, or taken out of your mind by someone else?

No, I've never felt anything like that. My thoughts are my own. Nobody is putting things in my head or taking them out, and I definitely don't think anyone can hear what I'm thinking. It's just their actions at work that I'm dealing with, nothing going on inside my own mind.
